title: A bounded-above complex of pseudo-coherent modules is pseudo-coherent
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $R$-modules. Suppose there exists $b\in\mathbf Z$ such that $C^i=0$ for every $i>b$. If each module $C^i$, viewed as a complex $C^i[0]$ concentrated in degree zero, is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], then the image of $C^\bullet$ in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. By [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m], each $C^i[0]$ is $r$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $r$. Iterating [lem-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent-shift] in either direction shows that $C^i[-i]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent: take $r=m-i$.

proof.text: Write $T_c=\sigma_{\ge c}C$, with original terms and differential in degrees at least $c$ and zero below. The inclusion $T_{c+1}\to T_c$ has quotient $C^c[-c]$. In each degree its sequence is either $0\to C^j\xrightarrow{1}C^j\to0$ or $0\to0\to C^c\xrightarrow{1}C^c\to0$; take the identity or zero as the sections and retractions. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] gives a distinguished triangle $T_{c+1}\to T_c\to C^c[-c]\to T_{c+1}[1]$. Since $C^j=0$ for $j>b$, $T_{b+1}=0$, which is $m$-pseudo-coherent using the zero finite free complex as witness in [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. Descending induction from $b+1$ to $m-1$ now proves $T=T_{m-1}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent: at each step the first and third vertices are $m$-pseudo-coherent, so the middle-vertex clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] applies. If $m-1>b$, $T$ is already zero.

source.place: Tag 064Y, lemma-complex-pseudo-coherent-modules, proof of the final assertion; Tags 064R and 064U.

proof.text: Let $L=C/T$. Explicitly $L^j=C^j$ for $j<m-1$ and $L^j=0$ for $j\ge m-1$, with induced differential (zero at the upper boundary). In particular $H^j(L)=0$ for all $j\ge m$. The zero morphism from the zero bounded finite free complex to $L$ is therefore an isomorphism on cohomology above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. This is an $m$-pseudo-coherent witness by [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent].

source.place: Tag 064Y, lemma-complex-pseudo-coherent-modules, proof of the final assertion; Tags 064R and 064U.

proof.text: The sequence $0\to T\to C\to L\to0$ splits in every degree: above or at $m-1$ its nonzero map is $T^j\xrightarrow{1}C^j$, and below $m-1$ it is $C^j\xrightarrow{1}L^j$. Choose these identity and zero splittings. By [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] it gives a distinguished triangle $T\to C\to L\to T[1]$. Both outer vertices are $m$-pseudo-coherent by the preceding steps, so [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle], middle-vertex clause, makes $C$ $m$-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: This holds for every $m\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] to obtain a bounded-above finite free model of $C$ in $D(R)$, which is the required pseudo-coherence.
